title: Disputes
description: Chargeback exposure, outcomes, the auto-resolve engine and response risk. The ratio bands are the CARD NETWORK thresholds, which are not the same as the warn and critical levels configured in /config. Counts come from the dispute mirror and the auto-resolve engine; money comes from the deduplicated money-out ledger, so it includes the per-chargeback fee that the dispute object itself never shows. The 'Billing: Support Events' dashboard answers what the TEAM did, and several of its events describe the same dispute.

panels.title: Open disputes

targets.query:
from(bucket: "${bucket}")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "dispute_snapshot")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "open")
  |> group()
  |> last()

panels.description: Disputes with staff work still outstanding, as of the last 5-minute snapshot.

panels.title: Due soon

targets.query:
from(bucket: "${bucket}")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "dispute_snapshot")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "due_soon")
  |> group()
  |> last()

panels.description: Respondable disputes inside the reminder window with nothing submitted yet. A missed deadline is an automatic loss, so this is the number to keep at zero.

panels.title: Blocked identifiers

targets.query:
from(bucket: "${bucket}")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "dispute_snapshot")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "blocked")
  |> group()
  |> last()

panels.description: Entries on the billing blocklist, mirrored into Stripe Radar.

panels.title: Auto-resolve pending

targets.query:
from(bucket: "${bucket}")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "dispute_snapshot")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "auto_resolve_pending")
  |> group()
  |> last()

panels.description: Refunds the auto-resolve engine has proposed and still owes an outcome: waiting out the veto window, or queued for the drain. Climbing and staying up means the drain is not running.

panels.title: Dispute ratio (month, VAMP)

targets.query:
from(bucket: "${bucket}")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "dispute_snapshot")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "vamp_month_pct")
  |> group()
  |> last()

panels.description: The month-to-date VAMP-style ratio, which is the figure the card networks actually judge. Updated on the dispute looper tick, not every 5 minutes, so it is a 6-hourly series by design.

panels.title: Dispute ratio (30d)

targets.query:
from(bucket: "${bucket}")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "dispute_snapshot")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "plain_30d_pct")
  |> group()
  |> last()

panels.description: The plain 30-day ratio. Lower than the VAMP figure because it counts differently; do not compare the two against the same threshold.

panels.title: Dispute ratio against the network thresholds

targets.query:
from(bucket: "${bucket}")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "dispute_snapshot")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "plain_30d_pct" or r._field == "vamp_30d_pct" or r._field == "vamp_month_pct")
  |> keep(columns: ["_time", "_value", "_field"])
  |> group(columns: ["_field"])
  |> aggregateWindow(every: 6h, fn: max, createEmpty: false)

panels.description: All three ratio figures on one axis, with the card-network warning and excessive bands marked. These bands are the NETWORK thresholds, not the ones in /config: the bot's own warn and critical levels are set per deployment and fire the Discord alert, while these are the levels at which a monitoring programme starts costing real money. Sourced from the 6-hourly dispute looper tick.

panels.title: Queue over time

targets.query:
from(bucket: "${bucket}")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "dispute_snapshot")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "open" or r._field == "due_soon" or r._field == "blocked" or r._field == "auto_resolve_pending")
  |> keep(columns: ["_time", "_value", "_field"])
  |> group(columns: ["_field"])
  |> aggregateWindow(every: 1h, fn: max, createEmpty: false)

panels.description: Open, due soon, blocked and pending auto-resolve, from the 5-minute snapshot. A due-soon line that never returns to zero is the shape of a team that is responding at the deadline rather than before it.

panels.title: Won
panels.description: Disputes decided in our favour.

panels.title: Lost
panels.description: Disputes decided against us. The money and the chargeback fee are both gone.

panels.title: Prevented
panels.description: Inquiries closed by refunding before they became chargebacks. A good outcome, but NOT a win: it never reached a verdict, which is why it is excluded from the win rate.

panels.title: Win rate

targets.query:
from(bucket: "${bucket}")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "dispute_outcomes")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "count" and (r.outcome == "won" or r.outcome == "lost"))
  |> keep(columns: ["_value", "outcome"])
  |> group()
  |> reduce(
      identity: {wanted: 0.0, total: 0.0},
      fn: (r, accumulator) => ({
        wanted: accumulator.wanted + (if r.outcome == "won" then r._value else 0.0),
        total: accumulator.total + r._value
      })
  )
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({ _value: if r.total > 0.0 then 100.0 * r.wanted / r.total else 0.0 }))

panels.description: Won as a share of disputes that reached a verdict. Prevented and warning-closed disputes are excluded on purpose: including them would flatter the number with cases nobody argued.

panels.title: True dispute cost
panels.description: Money withdrawn, minus what came back, PLUS the per-chargeback fees. The amount on a dispute object never shows the fee, and Stripe keeps that fee even on disputes you win, so this is the only honest total.

panels.title: Chargeback fees
panels.description: The penalty half of the cost above, on its own.

panels.title: Outcomes by reason

targets.query:
from(bucket: "${bucket}")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "dispute_outcomes")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "count")
  |> keep(columns: ["_value", "reason"])
  |> group(columns: ["reason"])
  |> sum()
  |> group()
  |> sort(columns: ["_value"], desc: true)

panels.description: Which reasons we see, across every terminal outcome in the window.

panels.title: Evidence submitted, by outcome

targets.query:
from(bucket: "${bucket}")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "dispute_outcomes")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "submitted")
  |> keep(columns: ["_value", "outcome"])
  |> group(columns: ["outcome"])
  |> sum()
  |> group()
  |> sort(columns: ["_value"], desc: true)

panels.description: How many disputes in each outcome had evidence submitted before they closed. Lost disputes with no evidence submitted are the ones that were never actually contested, and they are a different failure from losing an argument.

panels.title: Disputes by card brand

targets.query:
from(bucket: "${bucket}")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "money_out")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "count" and r.category == "dispute")
  |> keep(columns: ["_value", "card_brand"])
  |> group(columns: ["card_brand"])
  |> sum()
  |> group()
  |> sort(columns: ["_value"], desc: true)

panels.description: Which networks the chargebacks arrive through. Segment tags on money_out, so this reads 'unknown' for anything imported by a history backfill.

panels.title: Outcomes per week

targets.query:
from(bucket: "${bucket}")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "dispute_outcomes")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "count")
  |> keep(columns: ["_time", "_value", "outcome"])
  |> group(columns: ["outcome"])
  |> aggregateWindow(every: 1w, fn: sum, createEmpty: true)
  |> fill(value: 0.0)

panels.description: Verdicts over time, stamped at the moment each dispute closed rather than when we saw it.

panels.title: Reason against outcome

targets.query:
from(bucket: "${bucket}")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "dispute_outcomes")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "count")
  |> keep(columns: ["_value", "reason", "outcome"])
  |> group(columns: ["reason", "outcome"])
  |> sum()
  |> group()
  |> sort(columns: ["_value"], desc: true)

panels.description: Every reason and outcome pairing in the window. This is where a reason we systematically lose shows up, which is the argument for either better evidence or an earlier refund.

panels.title: Proposed
panels.description: Refunds the engine decided were worth making, before anyone could object.

panels.title: Executed
panels.description: Refunds it actually made. Each one should later produce a dispute_outcomes point with outcome 'prevented', but hours apart: do NOT add the two together, they are the same event seen twice.

panels.title: Vetoed by staff
panels.description: Proposals a human stopped inside the veto window. A rising veto rate means the engine's judgement and the team's have diverged, and the thresholds want revisiting.

panels.title: Blocked by a guardrail
panels.description: Proposals a guardrail refused. Not failures: this is the safety net doing its job, and the breakdown below says which one fired.

panels.title: Failed
panels.description: Refunds that were attempted and errored. Anything other than zero deserves a look at the logs.

panels.title: Spent on auto-refunds
panels.description: What the engine handed back, in each charge's own currency. NOT converted to a single currency, so on a multi-currency account read this against the per-currency split rather than as one number.

panels.title: Blocked by guardrail

targets.query:
from(bucket: "${bucket}")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "dispute_auto_resolve")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "count" and r.outcome == "blocked")
  |> keep(columns: ["_value", "guardrail"])
  |> group(columns: ["guardrail"])
  |> sum()
  |> group()
  |> sort(columns: ["_value"], desc: true)

panels.description: Which guardrail refused. 'none' appearing here would mean a block with no reason attached, which is a bug.

panels.title: Decisions by stage

targets.query:
from(bucket: "${bucket}")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "dispute_auto_resolve")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "count")
  |> keep(columns: ["_value", "stage"])
  |> group(columns: ["stage"])
  |> sum()
  |> group()
  |> sort(columns: ["_value"], desc: true)

panels.description: Inquiry stage means an actual dispute is open; EFW means an early fraud warning that has not become one yet. Refunding an EFW is the cheaper intervention, so a healthy split leans that way.

panels.title: Decisions by reason

targets.query:
from(bucket: "${bucket}")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "dispute_auto_resolve")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "count")
  |> keep(columns: ["_value", "reason"])
  |> group(columns: ["reason"])
  |> sum()
  |> group()
  |> sort(columns: ["_value"], desc: true)

panels.description: Careful: this tag holds TWO vocabularies. At the inquiry stage it is a Stripe dispute reason; at the EFW stage it is the warning's fraud_type, because an EFW has no dispute behind it to have a reason. Split by stage before comparing anything.

panels.title: Auto-resolve decisions per day

targets.query:
from(bucket: "${bucket}")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "dispute_auto_resolve")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "count")
  |> keep(columns: ["_time", "_value", "outcome"])
  |> group(columns: ["outcome"])
  |> aggregateWindow(every: 1d, fn: sum, createEmpty: true)
  |> fill(value: 0.0)

panels.description: Every decision the engine made, stacked by what became of it.

panels.title: Prevented against executed

targets.query:
from(bucket: "${bucket}")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => (r._measurement == "dispute_auto_resolve" and r._field == "count" and r.outcome == "executed") or (r._measurement == "dispute_outcomes" and r._field == "count" and r.outcome == "prevented"))
  |> keep(columns: ["_time", "_value", "_measurement"])
  |> group(columns: ["_measurement"])
  |> aggregateWindow(every: 1d, fn: sum, createEmpty: true)
  |> fill(value: 0.0)

panels.description: The engine's refunds against the inquiries that subsequently closed as prevented. These are the SAME events seen at two different moments: Stripe confirms the close hours later, so the lines lag rather than match. Read the shapes, never the sum.

panels.title: Evidence packs assembled
panels.description: Disputes we assembled a response for. This fires at most ONCE per dispute, either when a submit succeeds or when the looper refuses to auto-submit at the deadline, and the two are mutually exclusive: so this is a count of disputes, not a count of attempts.

panels.title: Auto-submitted
panels.description: Packs that went to Stripe without a human pressing submit. The remainder of the tile beside it is either a manual submit or a pack the looper declined to send at the deadline.

panels.title: Fields filled
panels.description: Evidence fields actually populated across every pack.

panels.title: Fields recommended
panels.description: Evidence fields Stripe recommended for those same disputes. The gap between this and the tile beside it is the evidence funnel, and a wide gap is the most common reason a defensible dispute is lost.

panels.title: Median hours before deadline

targets.query:
from(bucket: "${bucket}")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "dispute_response")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "hours_before_deadline")
  |> group()
  |> median()

panels.description: Typical runway left when we submitted. Small is dangerous: a response submitted an hour before the deadline has no room for a rejected file or a mistake. This value is NOT clamped, so a negative median would mean we are routinely submitting past the deadline.

panels.title: Tightest submission

targets.query:
from(bucket: "${bucket}")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "dispute_response")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "hours_before_deadline")
  |> group()
  |> min()

panels.description: The closest call in the window. Negative means a submission landed AFTER the deadline had passed, which is an automatic loss rather than a near miss, and it is deliberately not clamped so that it shows up here instead of hiding at zero.

panels.title: Packs by source

targets.query:
from(bucket: "${bucket}")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "dispute_evidence_pack")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "count")
  |> keep(columns: ["_value", "source"])
  |> group(columns: ["source"])
  |> sum()
  |> group()
  |> sort(columns: ["_value"], desc: true)

panels.description: Template, manual, or a mix. A template-heavy split is the point of the deterministic templates; a manual-heavy one means they are not fitting the disputes that actually arrive.

panels.title: Packs by reason

targets.query:
from(bucket: "${bucket}")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "dispute_evidence_pack")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "count")
  |> keep(columns: ["_value", "reason"])
  |> group(columns: ["reason"])
  |> sum()
  |> group()
  |> sort(columns: ["_value"], desc: true)

panels.description: Which dispute reasons we are assembling evidence for.

panels.title: Files attached by reason

targets.query:
from(bucket: "${bucket}")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "dispute_evidence_pack")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "files_attached")
  |> keep(columns: ["_value", "reason"])
  |> group(columns: ["reason"])
  |> sum()
  |> group()
  |> sort(columns: ["_value"], desc: true)

panels.description: Evidence files uploaded, by reason. Text evidence alone loses reasons that need a receipt or a delivery record.

panels.title: Evidence funnel per week

targets.query:
from(bucket: "${bucket}")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "dispute_evidence_pack")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "fields_filled" or r._field == "fields_recommended")
  |> keep(columns: ["_time", "_value", "_field"])
  |> group(columns: ["_field"])
  |> aggregateWindow(every: 1w, fn: sum, createEmpty: true)
  |> fill(value: 0.0)

panels.description: Fields filled against fields recommended, week by week. The two lines converging is the thing to aim for.

panels.title: Response runway per week

targets.query:
from(bucket: "${bucket}")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "dispute_response")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "hours_before_deadline")
  |> keep(columns: ["_time", "_value"])
  |> group()
  |> aggregateWindow(every: 1w, fn: min, createEmpty: false)

panels.description: The tightest submission of each week. A downward trend is a team drifting towards a missed deadline, and it shows up here weeks before it shows up as a loss. Values below zero are responses submitted past the deadline.

panels.title: Dispute events per week

targets.query:
from(bucket: "${bucket}")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "billing_events")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "count")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.event == "dispute" or r.event == "dispute_updated" or r.event == "dispute_won" or r.event == "dispute_lost" or r.event == "dispute_accepted" or r.event == "evidence_submitted" or r.event == "dispute_reminder")
  |> keep(columns: ["_time", "_value", "event"])
  |> group(columns: ["event"])
  |> aggregateWindow(every: 1w, fn: sum, createEmpty: true)
  |> fill(value: 0.0)

panels.description: What the team did, from the staff-attribution measurement. These events describe ACTIONS, and several of them describe the same dispute, so never sum them as money or as dispute counts. For money use the tiles above.
